card: Splits `tx_mempool_block_doublespend` unit test cases into independent tests with fresh state and makes the spends genuinely conflicting. Previously, shared mempool state required manual eviction between cases, and deterministic signing produced identical transactions rather than actual double-spends, causing the mempool transaction to be removed because it was mined instead of conflicted. This addresses a silent gap in mempool conflict unit test coverage. It touches only test code.
evidence: Author note in commit 19bb40c987: 'Both spends were built identically and signed with determinitsic nonces, so they were the same transaction rather than a double-spend. In the last case, the mempool transaction was therefore removed because it was mined, not because it conflicted with the block.'
Author note in description: 'Found during #36692: remove test state that is shared and modified across cases.'
problem: The four cases in `tx_mempool_block_doublespend` shared chain and mempool state, requiring manual eviction of mempool transactions between subtests. Additionally, identical transaction construction with deterministic signing produced identical txids, meaning the test was verifying eviction of an included transaction rather than a conflicting double-spend.

risk.why: A flaw in this change would only break the unit test suite or fail to catch a mempool conflict regression.

summary: Splits the `tx_mempool_block_doublespend` unit test into independent test cases with isolated chains and mempools. It also modifies the spends to have distinct output values so they are genuine double-spends rather than identical transactions.
